answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to stake a unique physical-world token verified by a distributed beacon network. For example, an opal gemstone embedded in a hardware wallet could serve as a non-transferable identity anchor, checked against a reef of trusted validators that cross-reference real-time sensor data. This makes creating fake agents expensive because each must acquire and prove possession of a scarce physical opal linked to the beacon.
